cues.en: Two out of the three fundamental
cues.zh: 关于我们在宇宙中位置的三大基本

cues.en: mysteries about our place in the universe have already been resolved. The first is literally about our place in the universe.
cues.zh: 奥秘中，有两个已经解开了。第一个就是字面意义上我们在宇宙中的位置。

cues.en: Many years ago, Copernicus told us that we were not at its center, that we were just a tiny dot suspended in the abyss. This is an image of the Earth taken from the probe Voyager one as it was leaving the solar system for about 6,000,000,000 kilometers away.
cues.zh: 多年前，哥白尼告诉我们，我们并不在宇宙中心，我们只是悬浮在深渊中的一个微小点。这是旅行者一号探测器在离开太阳系约60亿公里外拍摄的地球照片。

cues.en: All of human history, all of the history of life on Earth has taken place on that pale blue dot.
cues.zh: 整个人类历史，地球上所有生命的历程，都发生在那颗暗淡蓝点上。

cues.en: In the second mystery, Darwin then revealed that we humans are just one branch or one twig of a beautifully rich and delicate evolutionary tree and that much of the machinery of life is shared even with the lowliest of our fellow creatures.
cues.zh: 第二个奥秘，达尔文揭示了人类只是美丽丰富而精妙的进化之树上的一根枝条、一片嫩叶，而且生命的许多机制甚至与我们最卑微的同类生物共享。

cues.en: The third mystery is that of consciousness, our inner universe.
cues.zh: 第三个奥秘是意识，我们的内在宇宙。

cues.en: Now earlier this year, for the third time in my life, I ceased to exist
cues.zh: 今年早些时候，我人生中第三次失去了意识

cues.en: as the propofol anesthetic flowed from the cannula in my wrist into my bloodstream and then into my brain.
cues.zh: 当时丙泊酚麻醉剂从手腕的套管流入我的血液，再进入我的大脑。

cues.en: There was a falling apart, a blackness and absence.
cues.zh: 一切崩塌，一片黑暗与虚无。

cues.en: And then
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: I was back,
cues.zh: 我回来了，

cues.en: drowsy and disoriented but definitely
cues.zh: 昏昏沉沉、迷失方向，但确确实实

cues.en: there. And
cues.zh: 在那里。而且

cues.en: when you wake from a deep sleep, you might be confused what time it is, especially if you've been flying somewhere.
cues.zh: 当你从深睡中醒来，你可能会搞不清时间，尤其是如果你刚飞到了某个地方。

cues.en: But you'll know that some time has passed. There seems to be some basic continuity between your consciousness then and your consciousness now.
cues.zh: 但你会知道已经过了一段时间。你之前的意识和现在的意识之间似乎存在某种基本的连续性。

cues.en: But coming around from a general anesthetic, it could have been five minutes. It could have been five hours. It could have been five days or five years.
cues.zh: 从全身麻醉中醒来时，可能是五分钟，也可能是五小时；可能是五天，也可能是五年。

cues.en: I was simply not there, a premonition of the oblivion of death.
cues.zh: 我根本不在那里，那像是对死亡湮灭的一种预兆。

cues.en: And general anesthesia doesn't just work on your brain. It doesn't just work on your mind. It works on your consciousness.
cues.zh: 而全身麻醉不只作用于你的大脑，也不只作用于你的心智，它作用于你的意识。

cues.en: By altering the delicate electrochemical
cues.zh: 通过改变你头脑中精密的电化学

cues.en: circuitry inside your head, the basic ground state of what it is to be is temporarily abolished. And in this process lies one of the greatest remaining mysteries in science and philosophy.
cues.zh: 回路，存在之为存在的基本基态会被暂时抹除。而这一过程正包含着科学和哲学中至今最大的未解之谜之一。

cues.en: How does consciousness happen?
cues.zh: 意识是如何产生的？

cues.en: And why is life in the first person?
cues.zh: 而为什么生命是第一人称的？

cues.en: It is going away and coming back.
cues.zh: 它就是消失又回来。

cues.en: The modern incarnation of this problem is usually traced to Descartes who in the seventeenth century distinguished between
cues.zh: 这个问题的现代版本通常追溯到笛卡尔，他在17世纪区分了

cues.en: matter stuff, res extensor, the stuff that these desks are made of, that clothes are made of, but also that brains and bodies are made of, material stuff,
cues.zh: 物质材料，广延实体，这些桌子由它制成、衣服由它制成，大脑和身体也由它制成，也就是物质性的东西，

cues.en: and res cogitans,
cues.zh: 以及思维实体，

cues.en: the stuff of thought, of feelings, the stuff of consciousness.
cues.zh: 思想、感受以及意识的材料。

cues.en: And in making this distinction, he gave rise to the now infamous mind body problem. And life has never been simple ever since.
cues.zh: 通过做出这一区分，他引出了如今臭名昭著的心身问题。自此，生命就再也不简单了。

cues.en: But Descartes actually generated even more mischief with his doctrine of the beast machine,
cues.zh: 但笛卡尔实际上用他的动物机器学说制造了更多混乱，

cues.en: which I'm going to mention now because it anticipates
cues.zh: 我现在要提到它，因为它预示了

cues.en: where I'm going to end up as the bell rings when I finish in an hour.
cues.zh: 等我一小时后讲完、铃声响起时，我最终会落到哪里。

cues.en: Before Descartes,
cues.zh: 在笛卡尔之前，

cues.en: people commonly believed in something called the great chain of being with rocks and plants at one end and other nonhuman animals a bit higher up than humans
cues.zh: 人们普遍相信一种叫做“存在巨链”的东西，岩石和植物在一端，其他非人类动物比人类稍高一些

cues.en: and then angels and gods at the very top. And this great scale of being was also a scale of moral virtue so that humans had more moral
cues.zh: 然后天使和神在最顶端。而这个存在的巨大阶梯同时也是道德德性的阶梯，所以人类拥有比动物、比植物、比岩石更多的道德

cues.en: virtues than animals than plants and than rocks and so on.
cues.zh: 德性，以此类推。

cues.en: Now Descartes,
cues.zh: 现在说笛卡尔，

cues.en: he,
cues.zh: 他，

cues.en: in making this division between mind and matter, argued that only humans had minds and therefore moral status
cues.zh: 在做出心智与物质的划分时，主张只有人类有心智，因此才有道德地位

cues.en: while
cues.zh: 而

cues.en: other animals
cues.zh: 其他动物

cues.en: didn't have minds. They were merely physiological
cues.zh: 没有心智。它们仅仅是生理

cues.en: machines or beast machines, morally equivalent to plants and to rocks.
cues.zh: 机器或兽类机器，在道德上等同于植物和岩石。

cues.en: And in this view, the physiological mechanisms that give rise to the property of being alive
cues.zh: 在这种观点下，产生生命属性的生理机制

cues.en: were not relevant to the presence of mind or consciousness. And I'm going to propose,
cues.zh: 与心智或意识的存在无关。而我要提出，

cues.en: at the end of this talk, the opposite, that our conscious sense of self
cues.zh: 在这次演讲的最后，一个相反的观点：我们有意识的自我感

cues.en: arises because of and not in spite of the fact that we too are beast machines.
cues.zh: 之所以产生，正是因为而非尽管我们也是兽类机器。

cues.en: So to get there, let's return to the apparent mystery of consciousness.
cues.zh: 那么为了达到这一点，让我们回到意识这个表面的谜团。

cues.en: Now, recently as 1989,
cues.zh: 就在不久前的1989年，

cues.en: which is quite a while ago, but not that long ago, Stuart Sutherland, who was founding professor of experimental psychology at my University of Sussex, had this to say,
cues.zh: 那是相当一段时间以前了，但也不算太久，Stuart Sutherland，我所在的萨塞克斯大学的实验心理学创始教授，曾这样说，

cues.en: Consciousness is a fascinating but elusive phenomenon.
cues.zh: 意识是一个迷人却难以捉摸的现象。

cues.en: It is impossible to specify what it is, what it does, or why it evolved.
cues.zh: 不可能具体说明它是什么、它做什么，或者它为什么进化出来。

cues.en: Nothing worth reading has been written on it.
cues.zh: 关于这一点，至今没有写出任何值得一读的东西。

cues.en: It's quite a pessimistic point of view.
cues.zh: 这是个相当悲观的看法。

cues.en: And that may have been true then. I don't think it was true then. But in any case, things have changed a lot since.
cues.zh: 这在当时或许成立。我不认为当时确实如此。但无论如何，从那以后情况已经大变。

cues.en: And more or less about the time that Sutherland made these remarks,
cues.zh: 大约就在Sutherland发表这些言论的时候，

cues.en: we
cues.zh: 我们

cues.en: can see the birth or the rebirth of the study of consciousness within the neurosciences.
cues.zh: 可以看到神经科学内部意识研究的诞生或重生。

cues.en: And a good landmark is this paper by Francis Crick and Christoph Koch published in 1990.
cues.zh: 一个很好的标志是Francis Crick和Christoph Koch在1990年发表的这篇论文。

cues.en: And they start that paper by saying that it is remarkable
cues.zh: 他们在论文开头指出，值得注意的是，

cues.en: that most of the work in cognitive sciences and the neurosciences makes no reference to consciousness or awareness at all. And then they go on to propose their own theory of what the neural correlates of consciousness are, what it is in the brain that is responsible for being conscious. And since then, over the last twenty five years, there's been first a trickle and now a deluge of research on the brain basis of conscious experience. Some of this work is being carried out in my laboratory, the Sackler Sense for Consciousness Science,
cues.zh: 认知科学和神经科学的大部分工作完全未提及意识或觉知。接着他们提出了自己的理论，阐述意识的神经相关物是什么，大脑中究竟是什么负责意识。从那以后，过去二十五年间，关于意识体验的大脑基础的研究先是涓涓细流，如今已成洪流。其中一些工作正在我的实验室——Sackler意识科学中心进行，

cues.en: which was founded six years ago with Hugo Critchley, my co director. And there are now even specialized academic journals, The Neuroscience of Consciousness, which I started last year with Oxford University Press.
cues.zh: 该中心六年前由我和联合主任Hugo Critchley创立。如今甚至有了专门的学术期刊《意识神经科学》，是我去年与牛津大学出版社合作创办的。

cues.en: And this is a real change of the tide. When I started out
cues.zh: 这真正是潮流的转变。当我最初起步时，

cues.en: more than twenty years ago, it was thought to be career
cues.zh: 那是二十多年前，人们认为想要科学地研究意识是职业

cues.en: suicide to want to study consciousness scientifically.
cues.zh: 自杀。

cues.en: And it may still be. We don't know yet. Let's see.
cues.zh: 而这可能仍然如此。我们还不知道。让我们拭目以待。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: while the brain basis of consciousness is still a mystery, it is in some sense an accessible mystery.
cues.zh: 虽然意识的脑基础仍然是个谜，但从某种意义上说，这是一个可以接近的谜。

cues.en: And the author Mark Haddon put this very nicely, I think. He said, the raw material of consciousness
cues.zh: 我认为作者马克·哈登说得非常好。他说，意识的原材料

cues.en: is not on the other side of the universe. It didn't happen fourteen billion years ago. And it's not squirreled away deep inside an atom. The raw material of consciousness is right here inside your head.
cues.zh: 不在宇宙的另一边。它不是在一百四十亿年前发生的。它也不是藏在原子深处的。意识的原材料就在你的头脑里。

cues.en: And you can hold the brain in your hands.
cues.zh: 而且你可以把大脑握在手中。

cues.en: But the brain won't deliver its secrets very easily. What's extraordinary about the brain is not so much the number of neurons,
cues.zh: 但大脑不会轻易透露它的秘密。大脑的非凡之处不在于神经元的数量，

cues.en: though there are about 90,000,000,000.
cues.zh: 尽管大约有900亿个。

cues.en: It's not even the number of connections, though there are so many that if you counted one every second, it would take you about three million years to finish counting.
cues.zh: 甚至也不在于连接的数量，尽管连接如此之多，如果你每秒数一个，大约需要三百万年才能数完。

cues.en: What's truly extraordinary are the patterns of connectivity which, to a large extent, are still not known but within which are inscribed everything that makes you you.
cues.zh: 真正非凡的是连接模式，这些模式在很大程度上仍然未知，但其中铭刻着造就你的一切。

cues.en: The challenge is then this, at least the way I see it. How can the structure and dynamics of the brain in connection with the body and the environment
cues.zh: 那么挑战就在于此，至少在我看来是这样。大脑的结构和动态，与身体和环境相联系，

cues.en: account for the subjective phenomenological
cues.zh: 如何解释意识的主观现象学

cues.en: properties of consciousness?
cues.zh: 属性？

cues.en: And considering things this way, we come up against what the philosopher David Chalmers has often called the hard problem of consciousness. And the idea is this. There is an easy problem. The easy problem is to understand how the combined operations of the brain and the body give rise to perception, to cognition, to thinking, to learning, to behavior, how the brain works, in other words.
cues.zh: 这样考虑问题，我们就遇到了哲学家大卫·查尔默斯常说的意识的难题。其想法是这样的。有一个简单的问题。简单的问题是理解大脑和身体的联合运作如何产生感知、认知、思考、学习和行为，换句话说，大脑是如何工作的。

cues.en: The hard problem
cues.zh: 难解的问题

cues.en: is to understand why and how any of this should have anything to do with consciousness at all. Why aren't we just robots
cues.zh: 在于理解这一切为何、又如何与意识产生关联。为什么我们就不能只是机器人

cues.en: or philosophical zombies
cues.zh: 或哲学僵尸

cues.en: without any inner universe?
cues.zh: 而没有内在世界呢？

cues.en: Now there's a tempting intuition here, is that even if we solve the hard problem, even if we solve the easy problem,
cues.zh: 这里有个诱人的直觉：即便我们解决了难解的问题，即便我们解决了容易的问题，

cues.en: the hard problem would still remain as mysterious as it seems now.
cues.zh: 难解的问题仍会像现在一样神秘。

cues.en: But this just seems wrongheaded to me. It may not be necessary to explain
cues.zh: 但在我看来这想法是错的。或许我们并不需要解释

cues.en: why consciousness exists at all
cues.zh: 意识为何存在

cues.en: in order to make progress in understanding its material basis.
cues.zh: 才能推进对其物质基础的理解。

cues.en: And this for me is the real problem of consciousness.
cues.zh: 对我来说，这才是意识的真正问题。

cues.en: How to account for its various properties in terms of biological mechanisms
cues.zh: 如何用生物机制来解释它的各种特性

cues.en: without pretending
cues.zh: 而不假装

cues.en: that it doesn't exist at all, as you do if you solve the easy problem, and without trying to account for why it's part of the universe in the first place, which is sort of the hard problem.
cues.zh: 它根本不存在——就像解决容易问题时那样，也不去试图解释它为何从一开始就是宇宙的一部分，那算是难解的问题。

cues.en: And in the history of science, we've been somewhere similar before. It's hard to say if it's exactly the same situation.
cues.zh: 在科学史上，我们曾处在类似的境地。很难说是否完全相同。

cues.en: But in our understanding of life, eminent biochemists of the time found it entirely mysterious
cues.zh: 但在我们对生命的理解中，当时杰出的生物化学家觉得完全神秘的是

cues.en: how biological mechanisms could give rise to the property of being alive.
cues.zh: 生物机制如何能产生“活着”这一属性。

cues.en: And there were proposals of things like Elen Vitale and Essence Vitale and all sorts of other stuff.
cues.zh: 当时有人提出活力素、生命本质之类的东西。

cues.en: And although we don't yet understand everything
cues.zh: 尽管我们尚未理解

cues.en: about life,
cues.zh: 关于生命的一切，

cues.en: this initial sense of mystery about life has to a large extent dissolved as biologists
cues.zh: 这种对生命最初的谜之感，很大程度上已经消散，因为生物学家

cues.en: have just got on with the business of understanding the properties of living systems in terms of mechanisms.
cues.zh: 只是继续用机制来理解生命系统的各种特性。

cues.en: An important part of this story was the realization that life is not just one thing but rather a constellation
cues.zh: 认识生命的一个重要突破是：生命并不只是一件事，而是一个星群

cues.en: of partially dependent, partially separable processes like metabolism,
cues.zh: 由部分相互依赖、部分可分离的过程组成，比如代谢、

cues.en: homeostasis,
cues.zh: 稳态、

cues.en: reproduction.
cues.zh: 繁殖。

cues.en: In the same way, to make progress on the real problem of consciousness, it can be useful to distinguish different aspects or dimensions
cues.zh: 同样，要在意识这个真正难题上取得进展，区分不同方面或维度可能很有用

cues.en: of what it is to be conscious,
cues.zh: 也就是“有意识”究竟意味着什么的不同方面或维度，

cues.en: the space of possible minds if you like. And one simple classification is into conscious level
cues.zh: 如果你愿意，也可以说是可能心智的空间。一个简单的分类是分成意识层级

cues.en: which is the property of being conscious at all. For example, the difference between being in a dreamless sleep or under general anesthesia
cues.zh: 也就是是否具有意识这一属性。例如，处于无梦睡眠或全身麻醉下

cues.en: and being awake and conscious as you are now.
cues.zh: 与像你现在这样清醒且有意识的状态之间的区别。

cues.en: That didn't come up. Sorry.
cues.zh: 那个没显示出来。抱歉。

cues.en: Oh, there they are. And the conscious content, when you are conscious, you're conscious of something.
cues.zh: 哦，在这儿。还有意识内容：当你有意识时，你总会意识到某样东西。

cues.en: The myriad sights, sounds, smells, emotions, feelings, and beliefs that populate your inner universe at any one time.
cues.zh: 在任一时刻构成你内心宇宙的无数景象、声音、气味、情绪、感受和信念。

cues.en: And one thing you're conscious of when you are conscious is the experience, the specific experience of being you. And this is conscious self. And it's the third dimension of consciousness. Now I don't claim that these distinctions mark completely independent
cues.zh: 而当你有意识时，你意识到的一件事就是体验，作为你自己的那种特定体验。这就是意识自我。它是意识的第三个维度。我并不是说这些区分标志着完全独立的

cues.en: aspects of what it is to be conscious.
cues.zh: 有意识这件事的各个方面。

cues.en: But they're a useful, pragmatically useful way of breaking down the problem a bit. So let's start with conscious level.
cues.zh: 但它们是一种有用的、务实的方式，可以把问题稍微拆解一下。那我们从意识层级开始。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: What are the fundamental brain mechanisms that underlie our ability to be conscious at all? And we can think of this, at least to a first approximation, as a scale from being completely unconscious as if you're in a coma or under general anesthesia
cues.zh: 究竟是什么样的大脑底层机制，赋予了我们产生意识的能力？从粗略理解的角度来看，我们可以把它视作一个连续的光谱：一端是像陷入昏迷或全身麻醉那样彻底失去意识；

cues.en: to being
cues.zh: 另一端则是

cues.en: awake, alert, fully conscious as you are now. And there's various states in between being drowsy, being mildly sedated, and so on.
cues.zh: 清醒、警觉，拥有像你现在这样完全的意识。而在两者之间，还存在着诸如昏昏欲睡、轻度镇静等各种状态。

cues.en: What's important is that while being conscious and being awake often go together, this is not always the case. For instance, when you are dreaming, you are asleep but you're having conscious experiences,
cues.zh: 重要的是，虽然“有意识”和“醒着”常常同时出现，但事实并不总是如此。例如在做梦时，你处于睡眠中，但你依然拥有意识体验，

cues.en: the conscious experiences of your dreams. And on the other side of this
cues.zh: 也就是梦境中的意识体验。而在图表的

cues.en: diagram,
cues.zh: 另一侧，

cues.en: there are pathological states like the vegetative state where physiologically you will go through sleep wake cycles
cues.zh: 则存在诸如植物状态这类的病理状况，从生理上看患者仍有睡眠-觉醒周期，

cues.en: but there is nobody at home. There is no consciousness happening. So what are the specific mechanisms that underlie being conscious and not simply being physiologically
cues.zh: 但实际上却“空无一人”。根本没有意识产生。那么，产生意识——而不仅仅是生理上的

cues.en: awake?
cues.zh: 清醒——其背后的具体机制究竟是什么？

cues.en: Well, there are a number of possibilities.
cues.zh: 这里有几种可能性。

cues.en: Is it the number of neurons? Well, actually, probably not. There are more neurons in your cerebellum, this bit at the back of your brain, than in the rest of your brain put together. In fact, there are about four times more neurons in your cerebellum than in the rest of your cortex. But if you have damage to your cerebellum,
cues.zh: 是神经元的数量吗？其实可能不是。位于后脑勺的小脑，其神经元数量比大脑其余部分加起来还要多。事实上，小脑的神经元数量大约是大脑皮层其余部分的四倍。但如果你的小脑受损，

cues.en: yeah, you'll have some problems with coordination and other things, some cognitive problems, but you won't lose consciousness. It's not just the number of neurons. It doesn't seem to be any particular region in fact. There are regions that if you suffer damage, you will permanently lose consciousness,
cues.zh: 没错，你的协调能力和其他方面会出现障碍，还会有一些认知问题，但你不会失去意识。所以这并不单纯取决于神经元数量。事实上，它似乎也不取决于某个特定区域。确实存在一些区域一旦受损，你就会永久丧失意识，

cues.en: the intralamina nuclei and the thalamus deep inside the brain. But these seem to be more like on off switches than actual generators of conscious experience.
cues.zh: 比如大脑深处的丘脑板内核。但这些区域看起来更像是一个个电源开关，而不是真正产生意识体验的发源地。

cues.en: It's not even neural activity, at least not simple kinds of neural activity.
cues.zh: 这甚至不是神经活动，至少不是简单类型的神经活动。

cues.en: Your brain is still highly active during unconscious states, during dreamless sleep.
cues.zh: 你的大脑在无意识状态下、在无梦睡眠中仍然高度活跃。

cues.en: And even if your brain is highly synchronized one of the first theories of consciousness was it depended on neurons firing in synchrony with each other if your brain is too synchronized, you will lose consciousness. And this happens in states of absence epilepsy.
cues.zh: 而且即便你的大脑高度同步——意识的最初理论之一就认为意识依赖于神经元彼此同步放电——但如果大脑过度同步，你就会失去意识。这种情况就发生在失神性癫痫发作时。

cues.en: What seems to be the case is that being conscious at all depends on how different brain regions talk to each other in specific ways. And this is some groundbreaking work by Marcello Massimini in Milan about ten years ago. And what he did here was he stimulated
cues.zh: 目前看来，保持意识似乎取决于不同脑区以特定方式相互交流。这是大约十年前Marcello Massimini在米兰做出的开创性工作。他在这里做的是刺激

cues.en: the cortex
cues.zh: 皮层

cues.en: of the brain with a brief pulse of electromagnetic energy using a technique called transcranial magnetic stimulation or TMS.
cues.zh: 用短暂的电磁能量脉冲刺激大脑皮层，使用的技术叫经颅磁刺激，简称TMS。

cues.en: And then he used EEG, electroencephalography,
cues.zh: 然后他用EEG，也就是脑电图，

cues.en: to listen to the brain's echo. It's a little bit like banging on the brain and listening to its electrical
cues.zh: 来倾听大脑的回声。这有点像敲击大脑，然后听它的电

cues.en: response. And what he noticed when you do this you can see on the left is asleep and on the right is awake. This is very much slowed down. When you stimulate the brain in a sleep condition,
cues.zh: 反应。他注意到，这样做的时候——左边是睡眠状态，右边是清醒状态。这里速度大大放慢了。当你在睡眠状态下刺激大脑时，

cues.en: there is still a response. There's still an echo. But the echo stays very localized to the point of stimulation. It doesn't travel around very much. It doesn't last very long. But when you stimulate a conscious brain, there's a spatiotemporally
cues.zh: 仍然有反应，仍然有回声。但回声非常局限在刺激点附近，不会传播太远，也不会持续太久。但当你刺激一个有意识的大脑时，会出现时空上

cues.en: complex response. This echo bounces around all over the cortex in very interesting ways.
cues.zh: 复杂的反应。这个回声以非常有趣的方式在整个皮层四处回荡。

cues.en: What's more, the complexity of this echo can be quantified.
cues.zh: 更重要的是，这种回声的复杂度是可以量化的。

cues.en: You can apply
cues.zh: 你可以应用

cues.en: some simple algorithms to describe
cues.zh: 一些简单的算法来描述

cues.en: how complex, how rich this pattern of interactivity is. This is also from the Milan group. And what they've done here is they basically
cues.zh: 这种交互模式有多么复杂、多么丰富。这也来自米兰的研究团队。他们在这里所做的，基本上是

cues.en: look at the echo as it moves around the brain. And they see the extent to which you could describe it, the minimum description length, how much can you compress the image of that echo, much the same way that algorithms make compressed files from digital images in your phone.
cues.zh: 观察回声在大脑中移动的过程。然后看你能在多大程度上描述它，即最小描述长度，你能把那个回声的图像压缩到什么程度，这和算法用手机里的数字图像生成压缩文件的方式很相似。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: they come up with an index called the perturbation complexity index.
cues.zh: 他们提出了一个指标，叫做扰动复杂度指数。

cues.en: And what you find is you now have a number that you can attach to how conscious you are. And this is, I think, really intriguing because it's a first step towards having an actual measurement of conscious level. This graph on the bottom shows this measure applied to a variety of conscious
cues.zh: 然后你会发现，你现在有了一个可以对应到你意识程度的数字。我觉得这非常有意思，因为这是迈向真正测量意识水平的第一步。底部的这张图展示了这个测量方法应用于各种意识

cues.en: states ranging from pathological conscious states like the vegetative states where there is no consciousness at all all the way through locked in syndrome and then healthy waking.
cues.zh: 状态的结果，从植物状态这类完全没有意识的病理性意识状态，一直到闭锁综合征，再到健康的清醒状态。

cues.en: And you can immediately see that techniques like this might already have clinical value in diagnosing
cues.zh: 你可以立刻看到，这类技术可能已经在诊断方面具有临床价值，

cues.en: what
cues.zh: 可以判断

cues.en: potential for consciousness patients might have after severe brain injury.
cues.zh: 严重脑损伤后的患者可能具有多大的意识潜力。

cues.en: Now at Sussex, we are continuing work along these lines. We actually
cues.zh: 现在在萨塞克斯，我们正沿着这个方向继续研究。我们实际上

cues.en: look instead of bashing on the brain with a sharp pulse of energy, we want to see whether we can get something similar just by recording the spontaneous activity of the brain. So we look at spontaneous dynamics from, in this case, waking state and anesthesia. This is work with my PhD student Michael Sharn and Adam Barrett. We measure its complexity. And indeed, we find that we can distinguish
cues.zh: 不是用尖锐的能量脉冲去冲击大脑，而是想看看能否仅通过记录大脑的自发活动就得到类似的结果。所以我们观察的是自发动态，在这个案例中是清醒状态和麻醉状态。这是我和我的博士生 Michael Sharn 以及 Adam Barrett 合作的工作。我们测量它的复杂度。的确，我们发现仅凭大脑的自发活动就能区分

cues.en: different levels of consciousness just by the spontaneous activity of the brain. In a way, this isn't that surprising because we know various things change.
cues.zh: 不同的意识水平。从某种意义上说，这并不那么令人意外，因为我们知道各种东西都会发生变化。

cues.en: The balance of different frequencies of your brain activity changes when you lose consciousness. But this doesn't have to do with that. This is independent of that. There's something specific that is being detected by these changes in complexity.
cues.zh: 当你失去意识时，大脑活动中不同频率的平衡会发生变化。但这与那无关。这与那无关。这些复杂性变化检测到了某些特定的东西。

cues.en: More recently, we've applied the same measures to sleep. In this case, taking advantage with colleagues in Milan of recordings taken from directly within the human cerebral cortex. These are implanted electrodes.
cues.zh: 最近，我们将同样的测量方法应用于睡眠研究。在这种情况下，我们利用米兰同事的优势，从人类大脑皮层内部直接记录的脑电信号。这些是植入电极。

cues.en: And we see much the same story. If you compare where the two arrows are, you compare the complexity of wakeful rest and early non REM sleep where you're not dreaming very much, you see that complexity falls a great deal.
cues.zh: 我们看到的情况大致相同。如果你比较两个箭头所在的位置，比较清醒休息时和早期非快速眼动睡眠（此时你不太做梦）时的复杂性，你会发现复杂性大幅下降。

cues.en: What's interesting here is if you compare wakeful rest to REM sleep where people will often report dreams if you wake them up, the level of complexity is very much as it is during the wakeful state. There's something else going on here which is that the complexity in the frontal part of the brain seems to be higher than in other parts of the brain. That's something we still don't understand
cues.zh: 有趣的是，如果你比较清醒休息时和快速眼动睡眠（如果叫醒人们，他们常报告在做梦），复杂性水平与清醒状态非常相似。这里还有另一个现象，即大脑前部的复杂性似乎高于大脑其他部位。这是我们仍不完全理解的

cues.en: fully yet.
cues.zh: 地方。

cues.en: I just wanted to give you something hot off the press, so to speak, which is we've also been applying these measures now to data taken from people under the influence of psychedelic drugs, psilocybin,
cues.zh: 我想给你们一些最新鲜的信息，可以这么说，我们也将这些测量方法应用于从迷幻药物影响下的人身上采集的数据，裸盖菇素，

cues.en: ketamine,
cues.zh: 氯胺酮，

cues.en: LSD.
cues.zh: LSD。

cues.en: And what we find, at least in our hands to start with here, is that the level of complexity actually increases as compared to the baseline state, is not something we've seen before in any other application of these measures.
cues.zh: 我们发现，至少在我们初步的研究中，复杂性水平实际上比基线状态有所增加，这是我们在这些测量方法的任何其他应用中都未曾见过的。

cues.en: So what's important about this way of looking at things is that it's grounded in a theory
cues.zh: 这种看待问题的方式，重要之处在于它基于一个理论

cues.en: that tries to explain why certain sorts of brain dynamics go along with
cues.zh: 该理论试图解释为什么某些类型的脑动力学伴随着

cues.en: being conscious. And put very simply, the idea is this. And it goes back to Giulio Tinoni and Gerald Adelman people that I went to work with in America about
cues.zh: 意识。简单说，这个想法是这样的。它要追溯到 Giulio Tinoni 和 Gerald Adelman，他们是我大约在美国一起工作过的人，那大约是在

cues.en: eighteen years ago.
cues.zh: 十八年前。

cues.en: The idea is very simple.
cues.zh: 这个想法非常简单。

cues.en: Consciousness is extremely informative. Every conscious experience you have or have had or will have is different from every other conscious experience
cues.zh: 意识具有极高的信息量。你拥有、曾经拥有或将拥有的每一个意识体验，都不同于其他任何意识体验

cues.en: you have had or having or will have. Even the experience of pure darkness
cues.zh: ——你曾拥有、正在拥有或将会拥有的那些。甚至纯粹黑暗的体验

cues.en: rules out a vast repertoire of alternative possible experiences
cues.zh: 也排除了大量其他可能体验

cues.en: that you could have or might have in the future. There's a huge amount of information for the organism in any conscious experience.
cues.zh: 你未来可能拥有或可能获得的体验。对有机体来说，任何意识体验都包含巨量信息。

cues.en: At the same time, every experience that you have is highly integrated.
cues.zh: 同时，你所拥有的每一个体验都高度整合。

cues.en: Every conscious scene is experienced as all of a piece, as bound together. We don't experience colors and shapes separately in any way.
cues.zh: 每一个意识场景都被体验为一个整体，绑定在一起。我们绝不会把颜色和形状分开来体验。

cues.en: So conscious experiences at the level of phenomenology
cues.zh: 所以，在现象学层面上，意识体验

cues.en: combine these properties. They are, on the one hand, highly informative composed of many different parts. On the other, bound together in a unified whole. And this motivates us to search for mathematical measures which have the same property,
cues.zh: 结合了这些属性。一方面，它们信息量很高，由许多不同部分组成；另一方面，它们又被绑定成一个统一整体。这促使我们去寻找具有相同属性的数学度量，

cues.en: which are neither lacking in information.
cues.zh: 这些度量既不缺乏信息。

cues.en: On the left, you see a system which is all
cues.zh: 左边是一个完全

cues.en: connected together. So it can't
cues.zh: 连接在一起的系统。所以它不能

cues.en: enter very many different states. On the right is a system which is completely dissociated
cues.zh: 进入很多不同状态。右边是一个完全解离的系统

cues.en: so that it can enter states, but it's not a single system.
cues.zh: 因此它能进入各种状态，但它不是一个单一系统。

cues.en: We want measures that track this middle ground of systems
cues.zh: 我们想要能追踪系统中间地带的度量

cues.en: hit that combine both integration and differentiation.
cues.zh: 找到同时结合整合与分化的度量。

cues.en: And a number of these measures now exist. There are some equations here, which we can talk about later, if you like, that try to target this middle ground. And
cues.zh: 现在已有不少这类度量。这里有些方程，如果你愿意，我们之后可以聊，它们试图瞄准这个中间地带。而且

cues.en: time will tell whether by applying these more phenomenologically
cues.zh: 时间会证明，通过应用这些更偏现象学的

cues.en: grounded measures, come up with even more
cues.zh: 有根据的测量方法，是否能得出更

cues.en: precise
cues.zh: 精确的

cues.en: practical measures of consciousness.
cues.zh: 实用的意识测量方法。

cues.en: Now why is this business of measurement important? And I want to make a general point here, which is that if you're trying to
cues.zh: 那么，为什么测量这件事很重要？我想在这里说一个总体观点：如果你试图

cues.en: naturalize a phenomenon which seems mysterious, the ability to measure it is usually one of the most important steps you can take. And we've seen numerous examples of this. The history of our understanding of heat and temperature is one very good example.
cues.zh: 把一个看似神秘的现象自然化，能够测量它通常是你所能采取的最重要步骤之一。我们已经见过很多例子。我们对热和温度的理解史就是一个很好的例子。

cues.en: Here's an early thermometer from the eighteenth century which used the expansion of air. But of course, there are many problems in generating a reliable thermometer
cues.zh: 这是一支18世纪早期的温度计，利用空气膨胀。当然，要造出可靠的温度计有很多问题

cues.en: and a scale of temperature if you don't already have fixed points. And if you don't know what heat is, you get trapped in a kind of vicious circle that took a long time to break out of. But people did break out of this. And the development of thermometers catalyzed our understanding of heat from being something that flowed in and out of objects to being something that was identical to a physical property, the mean molecular kinetic energy
cues.zh: 以及温标，如果你还没有固定点。如果你不知道热是什么，就会陷入一种恶性循环，花了很长时间才摆脱。但人们确实摆脱了。温度计的发展催化了我们对热的理解，从某种流入流出物体的东西，变成等同于一种物理属性——平均分子动能

cues.en: of molecules in a substance.
cues.zh: 也就是物质中分子的平均分子动能。

cues.en: And having that concept of heat now allows us to talk about temperature far
cues.zh: 有了热量这个概念，我们现在就能讨论远超

cues.en: beyond the realms of human experience. We can talk about the temperature on the surface of the sun in a sensible way. We can talk about the temperature of interstellar space close to absolute zero. None of these things make any sense in our phenomenological
cues.zh: 人类经验范围的温度了。我们可以合理地谈论太阳表面的温度。我们可以谈论接近绝对零度的星际空间温度。这些事情在我们对冷热的

cues.en: experience of hot and cold.
cues.zh: 现象学经验中根本说不通。

cues.en: So this brings me to my first take home message. Measurement is important.
cues.zh: 这就引出了我的第一个核心要点。测量很重要。

cues.en: And consciousness, conscious level,
cues.zh: 而意识，意识水平，

cues.en: depends on a complex balance of differentiation
cues.zh: 取决于大脑动态中分化

cues.en: and integration in brain dynamics, reflecting the fact that conscious experiences themselves
cues.zh: 与整合的复杂平衡，这反映了意识体验本身

cues.en: are both highly informative and always integrated.
cues.zh: 既包含高度信息又始终是整合的。

cues.en: Now
cues.zh: 现在

cues.en: when we are conscious,
cues.zh: 当我们有意识时，

cues.en: we are conscious of something.
cues.zh: 我们总是对某物有意识。

cues.en: So what are the brain mechanisms
cues.zh: 那么，是什么大脑机制

cues.en: that determine the content of consciousness?
cues.zh: 决定了意识的内容？

cues.en: And the hero for this part of the story is the German physicist and physiologist, Hermann von Helmholtz.
cues.zh: 这部分故事的主角是德国物理学家和生理学家赫尔曼·冯·亥姆霍兹。

cues.en: And he proposed the idea that the brain is a kind of prediction machine,
cues.zh: 他提出了一个想法：大脑是一种预测机器，

cues.en: that what we see, hear, and feel are nothing other than the brain's best guess about the causes of sensory inputs.
cues.zh: 我们所看到的、听到的和感受到的，不过是大脑对感官输入原因的最佳猜测。

cues.en: And the basic idea is again quite simple.
cues.zh: 基本思路同样很简单。

cues.en: The brain is locked inside its bony skull and
cues.zh: 大脑被锁在骨质的头骨里，

cues.en: has very indirect access to the external world. All it receives are ambiguous and noisy sensory signals
cues.zh: 只能非常间接地接触外部世界。它接收到的只是模糊且有噪声的感官信号，

cues.en: which are highly indirectly related to this external world of objects and so on, if there is an external world of objects out there at all.
cues.zh: 这些信号与外部世界的物体等高度间接相关——如果外面真的存在一个物体世界的话。

cues.en: Don't know about that. Perception in this view is by necessity
cues.zh: 这我不太清楚。从这个角度看，感知必然是一个

cues.en: a process of inference
cues.zh: 推理过程

cues.en: in which
cues.zh: 在这个过程中

cues.en: the brain
cues.zh: 大脑

cues.en: interprets
cues.zh: 会结合对世界运作方式的某些先验预期或信念，来解释

cues.en: these ambiguous and noisy sensory signals with respect to some prior expectations or beliefs about the way the world is. And this forms the brain's best guess of the causes
cues.zh: 这些模糊且有噪声的感觉信号。这就构成了大脑对持续作用于我们感官表面的感觉信号成因的

cues.en: of the sensory signals that are impacting our sensory surfaces all the time. What we see is the brain's best guess of what's out there. I want to give you a couple of examples that illustrate this process. It's quite easy to do in a way. This first example is a well known visual illusion called Adelson's checkerboard.
cues.zh: 最佳猜测。我们所看到的，就是大脑对外界事物的最佳猜测。我想举几个例子来说明这个过程。其实做起来挺容易的。第一个例子是一个著名的视错觉，叫Adelson棋盘。

cues.en: Now here, you'll see two patches. You'll see patches A and B. And I hope to you they look to be different shades of gray.
cues.zh: 现在这里，你会看到两个方块。你会看到方块A和方块B。我希望在你看来，它们像是不同深浅的灰色。

cues.en: Do they?
cues.zh: 是不是？

cues.en: Yeah. They look to be different shades of gray. Of course, they are exactly the same shade of gray. I can illustrate that by putting an alternative image and joining up those two patches. You'll see that it's the same shade of gray. You may not believe me. So what I'll do is I'll shift it along and you'll see even more clearly. There are no sharp edges. It's the same shade of gray.
cues.zh: 是的。它们看起来是不同深浅的灰色。当然，它们其实是完全相同的灰色。我可以用另一张图来说明这一点，把这两个方块连起来。你会看到它们是同一种灰色。你可能不信我。那我把图移过去，你会看得更清楚。这里没有明显的边界。它们是同一种灰色。

cues.en: What's going on here, of course, is that the brain is unconsciously applying its prior knowledge that a cast shadow dims the appearance of surfaces that it casts onto.
cues.zh: 当然，这里发生的情况是，大脑在无意识地运用它的先验知识：投射的阴影会让被它覆盖的表面显得更暗。

cues.en: So we therefore see the patch B as being lighter than it really is in order to account for that effect. And this is, of course, an illustration of the success of the visual system, not its failure.
cues.zh: 因此，为了补偿这种效应，我们会把方块B看得比它实际更亮。当然，这恰恰说明视觉系统很成功，而不是失败。

cues.en: The visual system is a very bad physical light meter. But that's not what it's supposed to do. It's supposed to or one thing it's supposed to do is to interpret the causes of sensory signals in terms of meaningful objects in the world.
cues.zh: 视觉系统是个很糟糕的物理测光表。但这不是它的功能。它的功能之一，是依据世上有意义的事物，去解读感官信号的成因。

cues.en: It's also an example of what we sometimes call cognitive impenetrability.
cues.zh: 这也是我们有时称之为认知不可穿透性的一个例子。

cues.en: Even if you know the patches are the same shade of gray, when I take that bar away, they again look different.
cues.zh: 即使你知道这两块色块是同样的灰度，当我把那条遮挡条拿走后，它们看起来又不一样了。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: And people were expecting either that a patch was there or that it wasn't there in different conditions. And while doing this, we measured brain activity.
cues.zh: 人们预期，在不同条件下，补丁要么存在，要么不存在。在此过程中，我们测量了大脑活动。

cues.en: And to cut a long story short, what we found was that there were certain phases, certain parts of this cycle, this 10 hertz cycle, at which your expectation
cues.zh: 长话短说，我们发现这个10赫兹周期中有某些阶段、某些部分，在这些阶段你的预期

cues.zh: 对你所说内容的影响，大于你声称看到的东西。

And there's another part of it which was the opposite, where your sensory signals were more important in determining what you saw at that point. So this suggests
cues.zh: 这个循环有一部分是这样的。当算法进行时，其中一部分是你的预期主导了你的感知。还有另一部分则相反，在那一刻你的感官信号对决定你看到什么更重要。所以这表明

cues.en: that this oscillation in the back of the brain is orchestrating
cues.zh: 大脑后部的这种振荡正在协调

cues.zh: 这种预测的交换

cues.en: and prediction errors. And that's
cues.zh: 以及预测误差。而这就是

cues.zh: 成为神经机制

cues.en: for conscious vision. And other theories about what the algorithm is doing, there are many ones. One is that it's doing nothing. It's just the brain idling away. And I think this is at least more interesting
cues.zh: 关于意识视觉。还有其他关于这个算法在做什么的理论，有很多。有一种认为它什么都没做，只是大脑在空转。我觉得这至少更有意思

cues.zh: 来思考这个问题的一种方式。我们和另一位博士生 Asa Chang 做了另一个实验，我们给人们展示这些变化非常快的

cues.zh: 这些变化非常、非常快。这种学习的特征同样体现在算法中，这再次说明，这种振荡可能与大脑如何学习并更新对感觉信号的预测有重要关系。

cues.en: But we do not go around the world looking at Gabor patches or rapidly changing things like this. We go around the world looking at people and objects. And that's what our visual world is composed of. So can any of these ideas say anything
cues.zh: 但我们并不会环游世界，去观察盖博尔斑或这种快速变化的事物。我们环游世界时，看到的是人和物体，而我们的视觉世界就是由这些构成的。那么，这些想法能否说明一些

cues.zh: 关于我们日常视觉体验的事情呢？

cues.zh: 我认为，这是神经科学面临的一个非常重要的挑战：走出实验室，

cues.zh: 比如，这是一个物体。我觉得它就在那儿。在某种意义上，我能感知到

cues.zh: 它的背面，即使我根本看不到。即使它的背面没有给我任何感官数据，

cues.zh: 我依然把它感知为一个有背面的物体。这该如何解释？在贝叶斯大脑框架下，一种解释是大脑不仅在预测

cues.zh: 感官信号

cues.zh: 一直在采用一些创新的虚拟现实或增强现实方法。我们的做法是引入一些虚拟物体。而这些虚拟物体，

cues.zh: 十分怪异。那么问题来了，大脑从这些物体中学到了什么？以及

cues.en: So that brings us to the second take home message, which is that
cues.zh: 这就引出了第二个要点，即

cues.en: is the brain's best guess of the causes of its sensory input.
cues.zh: 是大脑对其感官输入成因的最佳猜测。

cues.zh: 正常感知是一种幻想

cues.en: Now before I move on to the last section, I want to pay tribute to an unlikely character in a talk about neuroscience,
cues.zh: 现在，在进入最后一部分之前，我想致敬一位在神经科学演讲中不太可能出现的角色，

cues.en: which is Ernst Gombrick. Ernst Gombrick
cues.zh: 那就是 Ernst Gombrick。Ernst Gombrick

cues.en: was one of the foremost
cues.zh: 是二十世纪最杰出的

cues.en: historians of art of the twentieth century.
cues.zh: 艺术史学家之一。

cues.en: And it turns out that Gombrich's understanding
cues.zh: 而事实证明，Gombrich 的理解

cues.en: approach to understanding art
cues.zh: 理解艺术的方法

cues.en: had a lot in common with ideas in the Bayesian brain and more specifically with the idea that perception is largely an act of imagination or construction on the part of the perceiver.
cues.zh: 与贝叶斯大脑中的观念有很多共通之处，更具体地说，与这样一种观念相通：感知在很大程度上是感知者的一种想象或建构行为。

cues.en: And this is most apparent in his concept of the beholder's
cues.zh: 这一点在他“观者的”

cues.en: share, which emphasizes that the viewer brings an awful lot to the table
cues.zh: “份额”概念中最为明显，它强调观者在体验艺术作品时

cues.en: in the act of experiencing an artwork.
cues.zh: 会贡献非常多的东西。

cues.en: So he had this to say in his 1960 book, Art and Illusion.
cues.zh: 所以他在 1960 年的《艺术与错觉》中这样说。

cues.en: The artist gives the beholder more to do.
cues.zh: 艺术家让观者有更多事可做。

cues.en: He draws him into the magic circle of creation and allows him to experience something of the thrill of making which had once been the privilege of the artist.
cues.zh: 他把观者拉入创作的魔法圈，让观者体验到某种创作的兴奋，而这曾经是艺术家的特权。

cues.en: And I think for me, this is very powerful when looking at especially things like impressionist art. And here, one way to think about this is that the artist has reverse engineered the whole perceptual process
cues.zh: 我觉得，这对观看印象派艺术之类的东西尤其有力量。这里一种理解方式是，艺术家已经对整个感知过程进行了逆向工程

cues.en: so that
cues.zh: 因此

cues.en: what's there are not the objects, the endpoints of perception, but rather the raw materials,
cues.zh: 那里存在的不是对象，不是感知的终点，而是原材料，

cues.en: the patterns of light that engage our perceptual machinery in doing its work. And for me, this might be why paintings like this are particularly powerful.
cues.zh: 是光的模式，它们调动我们的感知机制去发挥作用。对我来说，这也许就是这类画作尤其有力量的原因。

cues.en: Now, the final dimension of consciousness I want to talk about is conscious self,
cues.zh: 现在，我想讲的意识的最后一个维度，是意识自我，

cues.en: the fundamental experience of being someone, being someone like you.
cues.zh: 也就是作为某个人、作为像你这样的人存在的基本体验。

cues.en: There are many aspects to our experience of being a conscious self.
cues.zh: 我们作为意识自我的体验有许多方面。

cues.en: There is the bodily self, the experience of
cues.zh: 有身体自我，即这样一种体验：

cues.en: being and identifying with a particular body, a bit of the world that goes around with you in the world all the time.
cues.zh: 存在并认同于一个特定的身体，那是世界中一小块始终随你在世界中移动的部分。

cues.en: There's the perspectival
cues.zh: 有视角

cues.en: self,
cues.zh: 自我，

cues.en: the experience of seeing the world or experiencing the world from a particular
cues.zh: 即从特定的

cues.en: first person perspective,
cues.zh: 第一人称视角看世界或体验世界的体验，

cues.en: usually somewhere in the body but not always.
cues.zh: 通常位于身体某处，但也不总是如此。

cues.en: There's the volitional self, the experience of intending to do things and of
cues.zh: 有意愿自我，即打算做事情并

cues.en: making things happen in the world of agency.
cues.zh: 在能动性的世界中让事情发生的体验。

cues.en: And these ideas are, of course, often associated
cues.zh: 当然，这些观念常常与

cues.en: with concepts of will.
cues.zh: 意志的概念联系在一起。

cues.en: Then there's the narrative self.
cues.zh: 然后是叙事自我。

cues.en: This is where the only until now,
cues.zh: 这就是那个直到现在，

cues.en: we don't have to worry about the concept of I. But when we get to the narrative self, there is now an I. There is a continuity of self experience from hour to hour, from day to day, from month to month, and from year to year that you associate a name with and a particular set of autobiographical
cues.zh: 我们还不必担心“我”这个概念的地方。但到了叙事自我，现在就有了一个“我”。从一小时到一小时、一天到一天、一月到一月、一年到一年，你的自我体验具有连续性，你把它与一个名字和一组特定的自传

cues.en: memories. And finally, there's a social self.
cues.zh: 记忆联系起来。最后，还有社会自我。

cues.en: The way I experience being me is partly dependent on the way I perceive you as perceiving me.
cues.zh: 我体验自己作为我的方式，部分取决于我如何感知你如何看待我。

cues.en: I'm just going to talk in the minutes that remain about the bodily self. This is something we're working on quite a lot in Sussex, the experience of identifying with and owning a particular body.
cues.zh: 在剩下的几分钟里，我只想谈谈身体自我。这是我们在萨塞克斯大学正在大量研究的内容，即认同并拥有一个特定身体的体验。

cues.en: And the basic idea I want to convey is again very simple. It's just that we should think of our experience of body ownership in the same way that we think about our experience of other things as well. That is, it's the brain's best guess of the causes of body related signals.
cues.zh: 我想传达的基本想法同样很简单。就是我们应当像看待对其他事物的体验一样，来看待身体归属感的体验。也就是说，它是大脑对身体相关信号原因的最佳猜测。

cues.en: And the brain is always making this inference. It's making its inference about what in the world is part of the body and what is not part of the body. But it has access in this case to other sorts of sensory signals, not just visual signals or tactile signals, but also proprioceptive
cues.zh: 大脑一直在做这种推断。它在推断世界上什么属于身体、什么不属于身体。但在这个情况下，它能获取其他类型的感觉信号，不只是视觉信号或触觉信号，还有本体感觉

cues.en: signals, the orange arrows here. These inform the brain about the body's configuration and position in space.
cues.zh: 信号，也就是这里的橙色箭头。这些信号告诉大脑身体的构型和在空间中的位置。

cues.en: And then also and often overlooked
cues.zh: 然后还有，而且常常被忽视的

cues.en: are interoceptive
cues.zh: 是内感受

cues.en: signals. These are signals that originate from within the body that tell the brain about the physiological
cues.zh: 信号。这些信号源自身体内部，告诉大脑生理

cues.en: state or condition of the inside of the internal physiological milieu.
cues.zh: 状态或状况，也就是内部生理环境的情况。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: you can think the idea is that our experience of embodied selfhood is the brain's best guess of the causes of all these signals put together.
cues.zh: 你可以这么理解：我们的具身自我体验，是大脑对所有这些信号原因综合起来的最佳猜测。

cues.en: Yeah, that's just to emphasize interoception.
cues.zh: 对，这只是为了强调内感受。

cues.en: An important part of this idea is that interoception,
cues.zh: 这个想法的一个重要部分是，内感受，

cues.en: the sense of the body from within,
cues.zh: 也就是从身体内部感知身体，

cues.en: should work along the same principles, the same Bayesian principles that we've been thinking about vision and audition previously. That is
cues.zh: 应当遵循同样的原理，也就是我们之前思考视觉和听觉时所用的同一套贝叶斯原理。也就是说

cues.en: our experience of the inside of our bodies
